requirement.stated: play button: cd into the workspace before running the command
authorComment: // Prefix a cd into the workspace so the command always runs in the
// correct directory. JSON.stringify quotes the path "safely".

issues: frontend/dist/app.js:9 — `cd <path> && <command>` silently aborts the command when the workspace directory is missing or stale, where the old code ran it unconditionally; depends on `workspace()` never returning a non-existent path, which I could not read.
frontend/dist/app.js:8 — `JSON.stringify` double-quoting is not fully POSIX-safe for paths containing `$`, backticks, or `\`; the "safely" comment overstates it.

frontend/dist/app.js:12 — the change assumes the terminal panel writes `command` verbatim to a POSIX sh; if the panel re-parses or re-quotes the value, the embedded `cd &&` may not behave as intended (panel implementation not in this repo).

const cases = [
  '/tmp/ws$dir',
  '/tmp/ws`back`',
  '/tmp/ws back',

];

  process.stdout.write(full + '\n');
  process.stdout.write('---\n');
}

publishedAllegation1.reason: The source code at line 9 unconditionally prefixes `cd <path> && ` when wsPath is truthy, with no path-existence check. The review_shell experiment (Source 18) confirmed that when the path does not exist, `cd` fails and `&&` short-circuits so the command never runs and produces no stdout — exactly the alleged silent abort. The pre-change code at Source 1 line 29 passed the bare command directly to Panels.select with no cd prefix, so the old behavior ran the command unconditionally. Whether this regression is reachable depends on whether workspace() can return a non-existent path, which is outside this repo, but the shell-level behavior is confirmed.
publishedAllegation1.remedy: Validate the path before prefixing (e.g. check existence), or switch to `cd ... ; <command>` to preserve unconditional execution (dropping the working-directory guarantee when cd fails), or confirm workspace() never returns a non-existent path and document the assumption.
